defects.summary: The instance lock was opened through normal path-following file APIs and acquisition did not require one ordinary filesystem link or bind the acquired descriptor to a stable path identity. defects.title: Runtime-control cache trusted metadata instead of stable document content

incident.evidence: The stale-cache path was reproduced with an isolated control file by loading an unpaused document, rewriting the same inode with equal-length paused content, synchronising it and restoring the original mtime. Device, inode, size and mtime remained equal while the cutoff loader returned the cached unpaused value. No production control, service, network, X or provider was accessed.
incident.explanation: This establishes that a locally published pause could be hidden by cache reuse; it does not establish that a deployed operator pause was missed or that a live remote action occurred.

defects.summary: At 4e548b0a, load_control built its valid-cache signature from resolved path, device, inode, size and mtime, then returned the cached document without reading current bytes when those fields matched. An equal-length same-inode rewrite with restored mtime could therefore change the control content without changing cache authority.
defects.impact: A process which had cached an unpaused document could continue to treat remote writes as enabled after a valid paused replacement was durably published with the same observed metadata. The new pause would remain ineffective until some signature field changed or the process restarted.

introduced.explanation: Commit 4a4afb4f introduced the runtime-control cache with a pathname/mtime/size signature; later revisions added device and inode but still permitted a cache hit without reading content. Its parent has no runtime-control cache.

chronology.event: The runtime-control cache was introduced with metadata, rather than current document bytes, as cache authority.
chronology.evidence: Git introduction of _CONTROL_CACHE and the early return in load_control

chronology.event: Exact-cutoff review rewrote an equal-length control document in place, restored its mtime and observed the cached unpaused value survive despite different current bytes.

detection.method: Load an equal-length unpaused document, rewrite the same inode with paused content, fsync it, restore the original mtime, prove the cutoff signature fields are unchanged, and read control again in the same process.
